title: Comparison of Pointwise Encoding Time Reduction with Radial Acquisition (PETRA) MR-Angiography with conventional MR-Angiography-Sequences for Follow-Up of intracranial Aneurysms in a real-world cohort
summary: Regular check-ups after treatment of a brain aneurysm is important to see if any part of the aneurysm remains or if blood flows again into the aneurysm. While angiography is the best method, MRI is perferred for routine check-ups. This is because MRI does not use radiation and does not requiere arterial punction. However, the implants used to treat aneurysms can sometimes interfere with MRI imaging. This study compares a new type of MRI sequence called PETRA with the methods currently used to see which one provides the best imaging for vessel assessment.

interventions.name: All patients with a treated intracranial aneurysm that have a clinically indicated MR examination. Exceptions are patients treated solely via coiling or stent-assisted coiling. Analysis of imaging parameters on the MRI data acquired at the examination and comparison to prior imaging if availlable. D

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Treated intracranial aneurysm with documentation of treatment method.
Clinical indication for imaging
Exclusion criteria:
Incomplete imaging or insufficient imaging quality.
